title: Sort Google Sheets rows with AI using clear column rules
h1: sort a google sheets range without splitting records
description: Ask a bot to sort a bounded Google Sheets range by one or more columns. Keep headers and related cells together and approve the row order first.
keywords: google sheets sort rows with ai
claude sort spreadsheet by multiple columns
answer: **put dispatch in due-date order, with every customer still beside their own job.** the bot can sort a google sheets range by several columns. later rules break ties, such as customer name after due date. include the full width of each record, with headers and totals outside. ask it to show the range and wait before reordering.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: sort records with all their columns.
what:
**a date must travel with its customer and quantity.** sorting one column can separate values that belong together. give the bot the sheet link, tab and full record width.

keep headers and totals outside the range. name the last row or ask the bot to find where records end.

put rules in order: due date first, customer second. the second rule only breaks ties in the first.
uses: **put dispatch in order.** sort by due date, then customer for matching dates.
**find attendees faster.** alphabetise complete records while leaving the header above.
**group the job list.** sort by stage, then scheduled date within each stage.

routine.message: every thursday at 16:30, inspect the dispatch tab in the ottervale joinery spreadsheet. find all current job records and include every record column. exclude the header and totals. propose sorting by due date ascending, then customer ascending. show the exact range and both rules here. ask me before you change anything and wait for agreement. sort only that range, then confirm completion here. never sort one record column on its own.
routine.needs: google sheets read and write for inspecting and sorting the agreed range
routine.output:
ottervale dispatch sort proposal
records: dispatch a2:f24
first: due date, earliest first
then: customer, a to z
header and totals excluded. waiting before reordering.

steps: **limit the access.** connect sheets with read and write for inspection and sorting.
**describe the table.** include its link, tab, full record width and where records end.
**choose rule priority.** name directions and tie-breakers. require a range preview and your agreement.
**follow a familiar customer.** their date and quantity should travel with them. pause the routine if the layout changes.
watch: **everything in the range moves.** include full rows of record data and leave headers and totals out.
**rule order changes the answer.** customer first gives a different queue from due date first.
**follow the data after sorting.** open a familiar customer’s row and confirm its date still belongs to it.

faq.q: can it sort by two columns?
faq.a: **yes.** put the rules in priority order. the second breaks ties where the first column has matching values.

faq.q: will sorting wait for me to approve it?
faq.a: **only if you tell the bot to wait.** the sending setting does not pause this edit. include an ask-before-changing instruction.

steps: ask for the full record range without headers or totals
name the first sort rule and tie-breaker

mistakes.fix: include the customer, quantity and every other record column.

mistakes.mistake: letting the header join the sort
mistakes.fix: preview the first and last rows before allowing the change.

tip.text: look at one familiar record after the sort. its date should still belong to it.

worked.before: otto sorts only the due-date column. the dates no longer sit beside their own customers.
worked.after: the proposed range covers dispatch a2:f24, with the header and totals outside. each complete record moves together.
